conviction_note: Found a small up-lean: the company guides conservatively. It guided Q2 normalized revenue at -3% to -2% and delivered -1%, and its Q3 guide implies roughly -5.6% normalized at the midpoint against Q2's -1%. Positioning adds to the lean: 10.7% of float short, calls bid (skew -15.8) and the stock 0.9% above its 52-week low. findings.finding: Coursera's post-merger guide has proven conservative on revenue. On 2026-06-23 it guided Q2 normalized combined revenue at -3% to -2% YoY and reported revenue at +56% to +58% (about $291.9-295.6M on Q2 2025's $187.1M). It delivered $298.6M reported (+60%), with normalized revenue -1%, beating the top of its own range. The Q3 guide of $364-372M implies about -6.6% to -4.6% YoY against a simple combined Q3 2025 base of $389.9M (Coursera $194.2M + Udemy $195.7M), a much steeper decline than Q2's -1% normalized (-1.4% in the 10-Q pro forma, $381.4M vs $387.0M). Consensus of $368.5M sits at the guide midpoint, so repeating Q2's beat pattern would mean about $372-375M, +1% to +2% over the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-29) revenue beat the guide top and consensus ($298.6M vs $293.6M) and FY revenue was raised, and the stock fell -14.72% close-to-close (intraday -18%, on margin, FCF and a Q3 EBITDA guide below consensus per Barchart https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3560499/why-coursera-cour-stock-is-down-today). Revenue beats have been sold on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus sits exactly at the guide midpoint ($368.5M vs $368M), so the street has not modelled the beat pattern that played out in Q2. If it had priced a beat, consensus would sit near the top of the range, as Telsey's $370.5M does.
findings.independence: Q2 actuals and pro forma: 10-Q https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001651562/000165156226000063/cour-20260630.htm (same company, different document). Udemy Q3 2025 base $195.7M: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1607939/000160793925000138/q32025pressrelease.htm. Coursera Q3 2025 $194.2M: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1651562/000165156225000056/cour-20250930xexx991.htm. The June deck also says YoY change would 'face further compression in subsequent quarters', so part of the steeper Q3 decline is real, not padding.

findings.finding: Adjusted EBITDA has room to beat. The June framework guided a Q2 adj EBITDA margin of 11.0% (about $32M on the guided revenue), and Coursera delivered $42.7M (14.3%). It also lifted synergies to at least $85M run-rate by end-2026 (from $80M) and the FY margin to about 14% (+100bp). The Q3 EBITDA guide is $52-56M; Telsey models $55M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 EBITDA beat of about +30% vs the implied guide came with -14.72%. The market traded the forward EBITDA guide (Q3 below consensus) and the negative FCF, not the beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Telsey's $55M already sits near the guide top, so a beat on the order of Q2's would need roughly $58M+. The stock at its 52-week low says the market is not paying for margin delivery.
findings.independence: The June margin framework is in https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001651562/000165156226000051/presentation_supplementa.htm, which finding 1 also uses. This finding rests on the EBITDA line, not revenue.

findings.finding: Enterprise, now about 47% of revenue ($140.0M of $298.6M in Q2), is weakening on the company's own metrics. Enterprise net retention fell to 91% from 93% the prior quarter and 95% a year earlier, and enterprise customers fell 2% to 12,107. Management calls demand 'mixed across customer segments, regions, and use cases' and has flagged about $50M of 2027 revenue dis-synergies concentrated in Enterprise. That makes the Q4 guide and any 2027 framing the main downside risk on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last three negative prints (Q1 2026 -11.56%, Q2 2026 -14.72%, Q3 2025 -12.88%) were each tied to forward guidance or enterprise and margin commentary rather than the reported quarter (BMO in April cited Enterprise weakness and NRR decline: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/coursera-nysecour-hits-new-12-month-low-following-analyst-downgrade-2026-04-25/).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock is -45% from its high and at the low. The unpriced part is whether NRR keeps falling below 91% and whether Q4 or 2027 commentary quantifies the dis-synergy drag, which would show up as consensus FY27 EPS ($0.33, +65%) being cut. That has not happened.
findings.independence: Skillsoft (finding 4) is a separate peer read on enterprise learning. The $50M 2027 dis-synergy figure comes from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001651562/000165156226000051/presentation_supplementa.htm.

findings.finding: Pearson's nine-month trading update (2026-10-22) showed Enterprise Learning & Skills underlying revenue +6% in Q3 and +7% for nine months, citing 'strong demand ... for outcome-based skilling' and 'strong demand for the verification of AI skills'. That is a positive read on enterprise skilling demand in the same quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history of COUR reacting to Pearson updates.
findings.why_not_priced: A UK-listed peer's segment growth is not on US small-cap edtech screens, and COUR has fallen since 2026-10-22 (-7.7% over 5 days). The business mix differs, though (vocational qualifications, assessment), so the transmission is weak.

findings.finding: Positioning is set for an upside squeeze on any non-disaster print. Short interest is 23.7M shares, 10.7% of float, 3.7 days to cover (2026-10-15), and the stock is 0.9% above its 52-week low after -7.7% in five days. Options pay up for calls: 25-delta skew -15.8 vol points, put/call OI 0.56.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last up-reactions came from depressed levels: +36.23% (2025-07-24) and +13.64% (2025-04-24). The stock also rose +11.8% on 2026-08-03 on a single Goldman upgrade, showing how the short base reacts to good news (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3619069/coursera-cour-shares-skyrocket-what-you-need-to-know).
findings.why_not_priced: The skew already leans up, so part of this is priced. What is not priced is the asymmetry of a 10.7%-of-float short at a 52-week low: the realised history (5 of the last 6 confirmed prints down) suggests holders still expect a sell-off, which is what the short base is positioned for.

findings.finding: The holder base rotated in Q3, and the large legacy seller is finished. Baillie Gifford went from 5.4% (2026-06-30) to 0 shares at 2026-09-30 (13G/A filed 2026-10-05), and NEA cut to 4.9% (13G/A 2026-09-24). Pale Fire Capital (Prague) bought 1,332,742 shares at $5.06 on 2026-09-25 and 1,000,000 at $4.61 on 2026-09-29, taking it to 28.8M shares (10.9%).
findings.why_not_priced: Part of Q3's slide to the lows was a 5% holder liquidating. That supply is spent as of 9/30, and a 10%+ buyer was absorbing it at $4.6-5.1. If this were priced, the stock would not have kept falling into the print on no news. It is a mechanism (finished seller), not a fundamental.
findings.independence: Baillie Gifford 13G/A: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001651562/000108887526000063/primary_doc.xml ; NEA 13G/A: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001651562/000107261326000805/primary_doc.xml . These are three separate filers' documents.
